h.select_rule: Choose 10 that together cover the most distinct mechanisms, edit fields and condition fields; prefer clear, falsifiable claims that go beyond well-known findings yet have a concrete mechanistic rationale; include both directions; drop near-duplicates and claims merely restating main effects.
h.strategy: Use the retrieved literature to identify what is already well established about main effects, then deliberately go one step further: propose conditional effects the literature implies but does not directly test, or where findings conflict. Draw on general mechanisms such as redundancy, bottlenecks, saturation, interference between components and compensation. Span many different edit and condition fields, propose some LOWER-direction hypotheses where a common edit is predicted to help less, and make each 'why' specific enough that a single comparison could refute it.

hyps.why: With edge 0 removed, node 1 has no input, so a conv on edge 1->2 carries no signal and the edit has roughly zero effect.
A skip from a dead node 1 to the output contributes nothing, whereas it adds a useful shortcut when node 1 is fed.
With edge 5 removed node 2 is a dead end, so a 1x1 conv on edge 1 has no effect on the output.
A conv on edge 5 is only useful if node 2 carries rich features, which a 3x3 conv on edge 1 provides.
Node 1 feeds the output through a strong conv, so improving its input is worth more.
The output already receives a strong conv path via edge 4, so an added skip is partly redundant.
Replacing the identity shortcut with a conv loses the gradient-friendly residual path, so the net gain is smaller.
The output already gets a strong conv from the input directly, so a second conv path shows saturation.
The identity on edge 2 already merges node 1 into node 2 cheaply, so the conv adds less than when edge 2 is none.
Reconnecting node 2 to the output with an identity makes edges 1 and 2 useful again.
